title: 6 Months vs. 6 Weeks
subtitle: Marketing at the Speed of AI
abstract: AI can shorten a first draft. The bigger opportunity is changing how a marketing team gets useful work out the door. Mike Huber compares the production of two editions of his marketing field guide, then shows how the same approach applies to a campaign: a clear brief, AI-assisted drafting, human review and a shared workflow. Attendees will work through a campaign example, calculate the time recovered after review and rework, and choose a first pilot. The session separates Mike’s project experience from published research and gives managers a way to improve throughput without losing their team’s judgment or voice.
outcomes: Map a marketing workflow with explicit human review and approval.
Calculate net time recovered, including briefing, review and rework.
Define a 30-day pilot with an owner, quality standard and business measure.
audience: Marketing managers and directors, with business owners and senior executives as a secondary audience.
format: 45 minutes including audience activity and 5 minutes of questions

title: Just Because You Can
subtitle: Choosing the AI Marketing Projects Worth Finishing
abstract: AI makes a new marketing idea easy to start. It does not remove the cost of review, maintenance or a divided team. Mike Huber traces how a book update grew into an expanding collection of websites, tools and training products, until a trusted advisor asked what the work was actually meant to achieve. Using that story and a positioning decision from his brother’s pool business, attendees will apply a project filter to their own backlog. They will define “done,” estimate the commitment beyond the first build and decide what to stop, so useful AI experiments can become finished marketing work.
outcomes: Write a measurable definition of done for an AI marketing project.
Estimate review, maintenance and opportunity costs before approving a build.
Use a project filter to make a documented go, test, defer or stop decision.
audience: Marketing managers and directors, with business owners and senior executives as a secondary audience.
format: 45 minutes including audience activity and 5 minutes of questions

title: Getting Found When AI Answers First
subtitle: A Repeatable Visibility Audit for Marketing Teams
abstract: When buyers receive an AI-generated answer, a website visit may never happen. Marketing teams need a disciplined way to see how their brand appears without treating a handful of prompts as a reliable ranking report. In this session, Mike Huber shows how to build a buyer-question set, record mentions and cited sources consistently, identify gaps in useful content and separate visibility signals from business outcomes. Attendees will practice with a clearly labeled example and leave with an audit protocol, a content-improvement brief and a 30-day test plan. The approach builds on search fundamentals and avoids promises of guaranteed AI citations.
outcomes: Run a repeatable AI visibility audit with a fixed question set and documented conditions.
Turn observed answer and source gaps into evidence-backed content improvements.
Report sampled visibility, referral activity and qualified leads as separate measures.
audience: Marketing managers and directors, with business owners and senior executives as a secondary audience.
format: 45 minutes including audience activity and 5 minutes of questions

title: One Customer Interview, a Month of Useful Content
subtitle: An AI-Assisted Editorial Workflow That Keeps the Evidence
abstract: Your customers already describe the problems your content should answer. The challenge is turning one conversation into useful material without flattening it into generic AI copy. Mike Huber demonstrates an editorial workflow that separates the transcript, approved evidence, interpretation and publication. Working through a clearly labeled fictional interview, attendees will build an evidence sheet, use it to draft an article and email, adapt approved ideas for social posts and plan a month of distribution. The session includes review standards and a practical measurement plan, so the output stays accurate, relevant and recognizably yours.
outcomes: Create an evidence sheet that distinguishes approved quotes, facts and interpretation.
Use AI to draft and adapt content without adding unsupported customer claims.
Plan a month of distribution with human approval and buyer-response measures.
audience: Marketing managers and directors, with business owners and senior executives as a secondary audience.
format: 45 minutes including audience activity and 5 minutes of questions
